findings.summary: docs/development.md's registered-scene table claimed `upstream/babylon-lite-corpus.json` carries the digests "proving it matches the pin". The digests are written from the corpus files themselves, so they prove immutability since recording and nothing about upstream -- the claim this branch measured false. Corrected in place rather than left standing beside a TODO entry saying the opposite.

The TODO entry said the drift survived with "both gates green", but `lab/lite/src/demos/break-mesh.ts` is an application file: only test/corpus-goldens.test.ts hashes `applications[].files`, while test/corpus-scenes.test.ts covers `scenes` and `modules` and never saw it. The suite was green; both gates were not covering. Entry rewritten to name the covering gate per manifest section.

The TODO entry carried closed-incident narrative -- what the rewrite changed, and the 0.000/0.000 parity result that docs/status.md already publishes and `status:verify` already checks. TODO.md's own header sends done work to status, the docs and git history. Removed; the entry now states the gap and what unblocks it.

The TODO entry described the upstream-fetch design from scratch without naming what the repository already owns: `downloadCached` (src/asset-download-cache.ts) already fetches raw.githubusercontent.com at `sourceVersion` and documents that a clone at that commit seeds it, and reference/exact-corpus-manifest.json already carries a second digest -- for `sceneNNN` alone, written by the same hand, so more recorded copies do not close the gap. Both now named, with the measured counts (358 of 456 entries determine their URL from `upstreamPath`; 77 are release-archive members).

Altitude: the corpus-versus-upstream check should be built now as src/verify-corpus.ts in the existing verify-* family rather than filed, since the URL builder, the cached downloader and the command shape all exist and a probe dereferenced five manifest entries against upstream at the pin to prove it.
findings.blockedBy: Full coverage needs an extract-from-pinned-release-archive arm that does not exist, for the 77 manifest entries that are members of the freedoom and LibreQuake zips. The other 358 entries are not blocked by any missing capability; this branch was scoped to the corpus drift itself, so the checker ships as its own change with its own proof.

findings.summary: Efficiency measured that restoring upstream's source is an improvement, not a regression accepted for purity: bbl::js::Tuple<N> is itself std::shared_ptr<std::array<double, N>> (native/include/bblite/js_data.hpp:903), so the tuple rewrite saved no allocation, and because a tuple cannot be null it pre-allocated `entry`/`exit` per triangle per plane -- 25,356,184 record allocations against 1,188,040, and ~772 ms against ~563 ms, for identical output. The rewrite's own comment argued for the slower form. No action beyond the restore.

A for-of shape probe emitted what it then declined. `emitTupleForOf` decides the loop's shape by RESOLVING its subject, resolving a call compiles it, and a declining probe left the whole inlined body in the stream while the shape that answered compiled the same call again. break-meshes fractured every mesh twice and retained 304 orphaned meshes (~27.7 MiB) for a `bbl_fn_fn142_result` nothing read; doom carried two dead inline bodies and 30 dead declarations. Neither gate could see it -- an orphan is never drawn, and bbl::js::Array's non-trivial destructor silences the unused-variable warnings. Fixed by giving the probe a rollback (Compiler.probeEmission), which also reinstates a facility whose two orphaned doc comments ("for a caller that may undo", "Drop every line emitted after `count`") were still sitting in the StatementLoweringContext interface with no members behind them. Generated-tree neutrality: 16370 of 16376 files byte-identical, the 6 that moved are break-meshes and doom with pure deletions -- 0 lines added, 0 modified, temporary numbering unchanged. The deeper fix, value-semantics lowering for records that never escape, was measured and declined: the cost is one-time setup, not per-frame, and markStoredObjectReferences decides reference-ness eagerly and syntactically at ~25 call sites, so demoting a record needs two-phase type emission.
